title: Anti-Artifact Object-Continuity Detection Taxonomy
source: Derived from the 'Anti-Artifact Object-Continuity Detection in Video' report (sections 2-8) attached to this repo's prompt-engineering request.
purpose: Reference schema shared by datasets/anti_artifact_examples.jsonl, the prompts/*.md templates, and scripts/validate_video.py -- used to QA AI-generated video (e.g. Runway clips for Pinterest/Etsy content) for continuity glitches before publishing.

artifact_types.description: A single object 'flips' identity between frames (changes color, clothing, material, face) even though it should have a persistent appearance.
artifact_types.primary_signal: persistent-ID tracking (ByteTrack); a lost/re-assigned track ID at an unchanged bbox location.

artifact_types.description: Small jittery color/pixel noise between frames, often from weak cross-frame alignment.
artifact_types.primary_signal: drop in frame-to-frame embedding cosine similarity (Temporal Consistency Score) without a corresponding freeze.

artifact_types.description: Video stalls on one frame (near-identical repeats) for an unnatural duration.
artifact_types.primary_signal: run of consecutive frame hashes within freeze_hamming of each other, longer than freeze_min_run.

artifact_types.description: A segment of video repeats periodically (A->B->C->A->B->C) or resets exactly to an earlier frame; includes non-consecutive near-duplicate frames.
artifact_types.primary_signal: non-adjacent frame hash comparison at fixed lags; exact match = reset, small hamming distance = near-duplicate, periodic low distance = loop.

artifact_types.description: An object or character inexplicably reverts to an earlier semantic state (an accessory reappears, a cut fruit becomes whole, a fall is undone) without the frames necessarily being pixel-identical.
artifact_types.primary_signal: state-machine / interaction logic check on known object states, or a near-match against an earlier frame hash.
artifact_types.event_code: E05_FRAME_RECREATION_RESET (state-level; not always a literal frame match -- see notes)

artifact_types.description: An additional instance of an object class appears without a valid cause (duplication, splitting).
artifact_types.primary_signal: tracked object count for a class exceeds the expected/prior count.

artifact_types.description: The count of a known object class doesn't match what the scene establishes or implies (e.g. a basket that should hold N items).
artifact_types.primary_signal: tracked count vs. an externally supplied expected count (--expected on the validator).

artifact_types.description: Sudden non-physical bounding-box/shape change for a tracked object: jump in position, size, or aspect ratio inconsistent with plausible motion.
artifact_types.primary_signal: frame-to-frame bbox center shift, area ratio, or aspect ratio ratio beyond threshold.

artifact_types.description: An object's location or interaction state changes in a way that skips the physically-required intermediate motion (teleport, unexplained relocation, reversed motion).
artifact_types.primary_signal: large normalized bbox center shift between consecutive tracked frames for the same ID.

event_codes.notes: Codes E03-E06, A_COUNT_MISMATCH, A_COUNT_CHANGE, B03, B04, and C01 are verbatim from the source report's event-code/severity table. That table's rows for E01, E02, B01, and B02 were blank in the source (truncated numbering gap between E03 and B03) -- this file fills them in with codes consistent with the report's own narrative (identity inconsistency in section 2, temporal flicker in section 2/5.1, bbox jump in section 3/6.1) so the validator has a complete 1-13 code set. Severity scale: 1 = informational, 2 = candidate (needs confirmation), 3 = high-confidence / likely real artifact.

B01_BBOX_JUMP_CANDIDATE.checked_by: detection_checks (large single-frame bbox move, no class/ID change)

B02_IOU_DROP_CANDIDATE.checked_by: detection_checks (IoU between consecutive-frame boxes for same ID drops sharply)

label_schema.description: Flat per-artifact label schema used by prompts/few_shot_labeling.md, prompts/chain_of_thought_labeling.md, and datasets/anti_artifact_examples.jsonl.

fields.scenario: free-text description of the video segment being labeled
fields.object: which tracked object/class has the artifact
fields.frame: single frame index where it occurs (use this OR frame_range)
fields.frame_range: [start, end] frame indices for artifacts spanning multiple frames
fields.event_code: matching code from event_codes.codes above, for cross-referencing automated validator output

dataset_record_schema.description: Richer per-video schema (Table 2 in the source report) for a full labeled dataset, as opposed to the single-artifact flat schema above.

fields.video_id: unique identifier of the video, e.g. "vid_00123"
fields.objects: list of {id, class, bbox[]} tracked objects
fields.artifact_labels: list of flat label_schema records for this video

tier_3_on_flag_only: segmentation (SAM2) or optical flow to confirm a flagged segment -- not implemented in scripts/validate_video.py, wire in as a fallback for E01/geometry flags if false-positive rate is too high
